mortgage.q1: How is the monthly mortgage payment calculated?
mortgage.a1: With equal payments, M = P × r × (1 + r)ⁿ ÷ ((1 + r)ⁿ − 1), where P is the loan (price minus down payment), r the yearly rate ÷ 12 and n the number of months. A 320,000 loan at 6.5% for 30 years is 2,022.62 a month.
mortgage.q2: What is the difference between equal payments and equal principal?
mortgage.a2: Equal payments (an annuity, common in the US and UK) keep the same payment every month. Equal principal repays the same part of the loan each month plus that month's interest, so it starts higher, falls every month and costs less interest overall.
mortgage.q3: Does it include property tax, insurance or PMI?
mortgage.a3: No. It shows principal and interest only. Add your monthly tax, insurance and any mortgage insurance on top to get the full housing payment.
mortgage.q4: What does the amortization schedule show?
mortgage.a4: For each year, how much of what you paid went to principal and to interest, and the balance still owed at the end of that year. Early years are mostly interest with equal payments.
mortgage.a5: No. Every number is worked out in this tab. Nothing is uploaded or saved.

quadratic.q1: How do I solve a quadratic equation?
quadratic.a1: Write it as ax² + bx + c = 0 and type a, b and c. The roots come from the quadratic formula x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a. The page shows each step.
quadratic.q2: What does the discriminant tell me?
quadratic.a2: Δ = b² − 4ac. If it is positive there are two real roots, if it is 0 one repeated root, and if it is negative two complex roots and the parabola does not cross the x-axis.
quadratic.q3: Why are some answers shown with a square root?
quadratic.a3: When a, b and c are whole numbers the solver keeps the exact answer, such as (3 ± √5)/2 or 1/2, and gives the decimal next to it. Decimal coefficients get decimal roots.
quadratic.q4: What are the vertex and the axis of symmetry?
quadratic.a4: The vertex is the turning point of the parabola, at x = −b ÷ 2a. The axis of symmetry is the vertical line through it. If a is positive the vertex is the lowest point, if negative the highest.
quadratic.a5: Then it is not quadratic: bx + c = 0 is a linear equation with one root, x = −c ÷ b. The page gives that root instead.

team-generator.q1: How do I make random teams?
team-generator.a1: Paste names, one per line or separated by commas, choose the number of teams or people per team, and press Generate. Press it again for a new draw.
team-generator.a2: Sizes differ by at most one, and which teams get an extra person is random too. The shuffle uses your browser's cryptographic random numbers, so every split is equally likely.
team-generator.q3: What if the names do not divide evenly?
team-generator.a3: The line under the list says how it will split, for example 10 names into 3 teams gives teams of 3 to 4. With People per team the number of teams is rounded up and everyone is spread evenly, so 12 names in teams of 5 makes 3 teams of 4.
team-generator.q4: Can two people have the same name?
team-generator.a4: Yes. Every line counts as one person, so add an initial if you need to tell them apart in the result.
team-generator.a5: No. The list stays in this tab and is not saved. Copy the result to share it.

screen-resolution.a1: The large number at the top is your screen's resolution in real pixels. It is the screen size the browser reports multiplied by the device pixel ratio.
screen-resolution.q2: Why is it different from my monitor's specification?
screen-resolution.a2: With display scaling (for example 125% or 150% in Windows, or a Retina Mac) the browser lays out pages in CSS pixels. 1920 × 1080 at 125% is reported as 1536 × 864 CSS pixels. Browser zoom also changes the pixel ratio, so reset zoom to 100% for the true figure.
screen-resolution.a3: The part of the browser window that shows the page, in CSS pixels. It changes as you resize the window and is what responsive web designs use.
screen-resolution.q4: What is the device pixel ratio?
screen-resolution.a4: How many real pixels make up one CSS pixel. 1 is a standard screen, 2 or 3 is common on phones and Retina screens, and 1.25 or 1.5 means display scaling is on.
screen-resolution.q5: Is anything sent to a server?
screen-resolution.a5: No. The values are read by your browser in this tab and are not saved or uploaded.

alarm.q1: How do I set an alarm online?
alarm.a1: Pick a time, choose a sound and press Set alarm. The page shows how long until it rings. Press Test sound first to check the volume.
alarm.q2: Will it ring if the tab is in the background?
alarm.a2: Yes, while the tab stays open and the computer is awake. The sound is queued in the browser's audio engine, so a background tab still rings on time. Closing the tab, sleep mode or a locked phone can stop it.
alarm.a3: Yes. When it rings, press Snooze 5 min or Snooze 10 min, or Stop. It stops by itself after 10 minutes.
alarm.a4: Check the volume and that the tab or site is not muted. Some phones mute web audio in silent mode. The alarm must be set with a tap or click, as browsers only allow sound after one.
alarm.a5: No. It lives in this tab only. Nothing is uploaded, and reloading the page clears it.
